questions.stem: Which CLZ-150 structure is intended for learner-supplied configuration values?

optionExplanations.A: Locals derive internal values rather than accept -var overrides.
optionExplanations.B: Addresses identify managed objects.
optionExplanations.C: It explains the system but supplies no Terraform inputs.
optionExplanations.D: Variables define the module's public input interface.

questions.stem: Which expression references the derived naming prefix in CLZ-150?

optionExplanations.A: The local namespace exposes named local values.
optionExplanations.B: That is not a valid reference to this local.
optionExplanations.C: Outputs do not use this namespace.
optionExplanations.D: The resource is named lab, not prefix.

questions.stem: What happens when a learner tries to override local.lab_id using -var?

options.B: It is not a declared input to override that way.
options.D: It silently renames all lessons in the repository.

optionExplanations.A: Locals are not command-line input variables.
optionExplanations.B: Change supported input values, not an undeclared variable assignment.
optionExplanations.C: Lesson IDs do not select a directory.
optionExplanations.D: The CLI evaluates the current module only.

questions.stem: What is the role of output resource_group_name in this lesson?

options.C: Expose the deployed group's name for validation and scripts.

optionExplanations.A: Input defaults are declared in variable blocks.
optionExplanations.B: Provider installation belongs to init.
optionExplanations.C: It is an observable result of the managed resource.
optionExplanations.D: The output exposes a result; the resource property is configured separately.

questions.stem: Which environment input is accepted by CLZ-150's contains validation?

optionExplanations.A: The documented string is prod.
optionExplanations.B: Staging is not in the allowed set.
optionExplanations.C: The allowed strings are lowercase.
optionExplanations.D: The list permits dev, test, and prod.

questions.stem: Why use terraform output -json with ConvertFrom-Json?

options.A: To parse stored output values and metadata in PowerShell.
options.B: To automatically deploy all JSON keys.

optionExplanations.A: JSON is suitable for structured consumption.
optionExplanations.B: Parsing output does not apply resources.
optionExplanations.C: JSON serialization is not encryption.
optionExplanations.D: Outputs do not change input declarations.

questions.stem: An output depends on a value Azure assigns during creation and appears unknown in plan. What does that mean?

options.A: The output block is always invalid.
options.B: Terraform expects the value to become available after apply.
options.D: The value must be hardcoded into state.

optionExplanations.A: Unknown planned values can be valid.
optionExplanations.B: Some provider results are not known during planning.
optionExplanations.C: Unknown output text does not prove that.
optionExplanations.D: Do not manually edit state to invent a result.

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of using local.tags across multiple resource declarations?

options.A: It prevents all Azure Policy effects.
options.C: One shared expression keeps metadata consistent.

optionExplanations.A: Policies still apply.
optionExplanations.B: Configuration can be changed and applied.
optionExplanations.C: Consumers can reference the same derived map.
optionExplanations.D: Locals are not an encryption feature.

questions.stem: environment=dev is the declared default, but the plan supplies -var='environment=test'. Which value does that input use?

optionExplanations.A: The default applies when no higher-precedence value is supplied.
optionExplanations.B: The string input has one selected value.
optionExplanations.C: No input source supplied prod.
optionExplanations.D: An explicit command-line assignment overrides the default.

questions.stem: Which added output best fits this lesson's validation-friendly public results?

options.D: A shared client secret in plaintext.

optionExplanations.A: It is useful and does not contain a credential.
optionExplanations.B: Credentials do not belong in a public result.
optionExplanations.C: That would expose secret data.
optionExplanations.D: It is not a safe validation interface.

questions.stem: A production author marks an output sensitive. What protection does that provide?

options.A: Automatic state encryption in every backend.
options.B: Redaction in ordinary displays, not removal from state.
options.C: Permanent prevention of all raw output access.
options.D: Deletion of the secret from Azure.

optionExplanations.A: The sensitive flag is not backend encryption.
optionExplanations.B: Sensitive values can remain in Terraform artifacts.
optionExplanations.C: Explicit raw/JSON output can reveal values.
optionExplanations.D: The flag is display/data-flow metadata.

questions.stem: Which command opens the interactive evaluator used to inspect local.prefix?

optionExplanations.A: That changes CLI context.
optionExplanations.B: That removes state bindings.
optionExplanations.C: Console evaluates expressions in the current module.
optionExplanations.D: That removes managed resources.

questions.stem: Why declare name_prefix as type=string?

options.B: To guarantee the name exists in Azure.
options.C: To prohibit using the input in locals.
options.D: To constrain the input interface to a string value.

optionExplanations.A: A type declaration does not create resources.
optionExplanations.B: Type checking is not a cloud lookup.
optionExplanations.C: Locals can reference inputs.
optionExplanations.D: Type constraints clarify and validate module arguments.

questions.stem: A learner wants a different prefix without editing local.prefix. What is the supported approach?

options.A: Change name_prefix or environment, then review a plan.

optionExplanations.A: The local expression derives its value from those inputs.
optionExplanations.B: No prefix input is declared.
optionExplanations.C: State is not the input interface.
optionExplanations.D: Filename changes do not alter the expression.

questions.stem: In a reusable production module, why document renamed inputs and outputs as breaking changes?

options.A: Azure forces every output to have the same name.
options.B: Consumers may depend on the existing interface.
options.C: A renamed output grants new permissions.
options.D: The website will automatically migrate all callers.

optionExplanations.A: Output names are authored in Terraform.
optionExplanations.B: Inputs and outputs form a contract between modules and callers.
optionExplanations.C: Names do not grant RBAC roles.
optionExplanations.D: Documentation cannot update Terraform consumers automatically.

questions.stem: The subscription variable permits null but its validation checks non-null values for GUID shape. Which result matches that design?

optionExplanations.A: No conversion is defined.
optionExplanations.B: Input validation does not provision subscriptions.
optionExplanations.C: The conditional explicitly permits it.
optionExplanations.D: Environment selection is separate.

questions.stem: A location passes the configured lowercase/alphanumeric regex. What does that prove?

options.A: The region supports every VM size.
options.D: It satisfies the local format rule.

optionExplanations.A: Availability is external evidence.
optionExplanations.B: Quota requires separate inspection.
optionExplanations.C: RBAC is not a string-pattern test.
optionExplanations.D: The pattern does not query the Azure region catalog.

questions.stem: Where does the location output get its value in the supplied module?

optionExplanations.A: It exposes the managed group's location attribute.
optionExplanations.B: Environment and location are separate properties.
optionExplanations.C: This output references the managed resource attribute, not a provider default-region setting.
optionExplanations.D: Hostnames do not supply this output.

questions.stem: Why does the lab reject name_prefix='TEAM'?

options.A: All Terraform strings must be lowercase.
options.B: Its validation requires lowercase permitted characters.
options.D: The prefix must be a GUID.

optionExplanations.A: Terraform supports uppercase strings in general.
optionExplanations.B: The regex encodes the intended naming interface.
optionExplanations.C: That is not the cause here.
optionExplanations.D: Only subscription_id has the GUID format.

questions.stem: Which fixed code must appear in local.prefix for CLZ-150?

optionExplanations.A: That belongs to the previous lesson.
optionExplanations.B: The prefix also includes the lesson code.
optionExplanations.C: It derives from the local CLZ-150 identifier.
optionExplanations.D: Tenant metadata is not part of this expression.

questions.stem: Why copy terraform.tfvars.example to an untracked local terraform.tfvars?

options.D: To supply local inputs without rewriting the shared template.

optionExplanations.A: Copying a file does not authenticate.
optionExplanations.B: tfvars and lock files serve different purposes.
optionExplanations.C: Input-file placement does not mark outputs sensitive.
optionExplanations.D: The template documents placeholders and example values.

questions.stem: Which declaration accepts a caller's environment choice rather than returns a result?

optionExplanations.A: Variable blocks define incoming arguments.
optionExplanations.B: Outputs return evaluated results.
optionExplanations.C: That is a result interface.
optionExplanations.D: That is internal derived data.

questions.stem: The Environment tag changes after environment=test is supplied. Why?

options.A: Azure guesses the environment from the user.
options.C: Changing a variable automatically edits every source file.
options.D: The Terraform output command changes tags.

optionExplanations.A: The value is explicit configuration.
optionExplanations.B: The map is computed from the selected input.
optionExplanations.C: Evaluation does not rewrite Terraform source.
optionExplanations.D: Reading outputs is not an Azure write.

questions.stem: What does evaluating local.tags in terraform console do?

options.A: Apply each tag to every subscription.
options.C: Display the evaluated map without applying Azure changes.

optionExplanations.A: Console does not run a resource apply.
optionExplanations.B: No apply happens.
optionExplanations.C: Expression evaluation is not resource deployment.
optionExplanations.D: No backend migration is invoked.

questions.stem: A learner adds a custom value to tfvars but no corresponding variable declaration. What should a reusable module author do?

options.A: Assume every file key is an implicit local.
options.B: Embed the value in state JSON.
options.C: Add only a matching output block.
options.D: Declare and document a supported input if it is needed.

optionExplanations.A: Terraform does not create locals from arbitrary keys.
optionExplanations.B: State is not a public argument contract.
optionExplanations.C: An output exposes a result rather than declares an accepted input.
optionExplanations.D: The interface should explicitly define accepted arguments.

questions.stem: The output name references the managed resource rather than duplicates its naming string. What does that achieve?

options.A: It exposes the resource's actual attribute through its dependency.
options.B: It prevents Terraform from tracking the resource.
options.C: It moves the object into another subscription.
options.D: It makes group tags inherit everywhere.

optionExplanations.A: The result follows the managed object.
optionExplanations.B: Resource references create dependencies, not remove tracking.
optionExplanations.C: A reference does not change target context.
optionExplanations.D: Tag inheritance is unrelated.

questions.stem: A script only needs the group's name. Which output mode avoids parsing the complete JSON object?

optionExplanations.A: That emits structured JSON rather than a single raw value.
optionExplanations.B: It emits the named scalar for shell use.
optionExplanations.C: That reports schema metadata.
optionExplanations.D: That reads the directory ID.

questions.stem: Which production module change best reflects this lesson's separation of concerns?

options.A: Place every value in outputs and accept no inputs.
options.B: Duplicate naming expressions in every resource.
options.C: Document inputs, derive repeated expressions in locals, and expose intentional outputs.
options.D: Treat state JSON as the only public API.

optionExplanations.A: Outputs are not caller-supplied arguments.
optionExplanations.B: That increases inconsistency risk.
optionExplanations.C: These layers keep the configuration understandable.
optionExplanations.D: State is not the intended module interface.

questions.stem: After CLZ-150 cleanup, which result is expected for the managed-resource inventory?

options.B: The dependency lock file is deleted.

optionExplanations.A: Destroy does not rewrite locals.tf.
optionExplanations.B: Keep the committed dependency file.
optionExplanations.C: Configuration declarations remain.
optionExplanations.D: The group's state binding is removed by successful destroy.

questions.learningObjective: Use validation to reject bad input
questions.stem: The exercise adds a custom prefix validation. How should the learner test it safely?

options.A: Run a plan with an intentionally invalid value and expect rejection.
options.C: Edit state until the value looks valid.

optionExplanations.A: The check should fail before apply.
optionExplanations.B: That bypasses the purpose of pre-deployment validation.
optionExplanations.C: Do not fake input acceptance in state.
optionExplanations.D: That weakens rather than tests the interface.
